newsitem.title: JAPAN: Santer says sees 'substantial number' joining Euro.
newsitem.headline: Santer says sees 'substantial number' joining Euro.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said on Friday that he was confident a "substantial number" of countries would join Europe's single currency at the initial stage.

Santer, speaking to reporters at the end of a five-day visit to Japan, reiterated that Europe's Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) was on track for introduction of the new single currency by January 1, 1999, on the basis of "the strict criteria of stability and convergence".
"There is not only a political willingness but also concrete results" to achieve the criteria for EMU membership as defined by the 1992 Maastricht treaty, he said.
Santer, who met Japanese officials, business executives and politicians during his visit, said Europe was keen to see Japan continue to deregulate its economy.
Santer noted that Europe's trade deficit with Japan had improved, but added that "several market access issues remain to be solved".

Commenting on the World Trade Organisation's (WTO) ministerial meeting to be held in Singapore in December, he said: "I think Japan and the European Union have the same interest to oppose the unilateralist tendencies of some other partners."
